title: FT-MUX: A Fault-Tolerant Microfluidic Multiplexer Design
problem: Microfluidic multiplexers enable routing through many flow channels with few control channels, but as integration scales up, control-channel defects affect large numbers of flow channels, creating reliability concerns.
motivation: Microfluidic devices scale to higher integration, making fault tolerance in critical routing structures essential for yield and reliability.
method: FT-MUX analyzes how to design multiplexers that keep working when control channels break. It models this using coding theory—the mathematical framework that makes error-correcting codes work—specifically as a binary constant weight code to find efficient designs that minimize wasted resources. This reveals design rules that ensure the multiplexer functions with up to n defective control channels. The result is that fault-tolerant designs can actually route fluids through more channels than standard multiplexers, even with equal or fewer control channels.
key_novelty: FT-MUX is the first framework that uses coding theory to formally design microfluidic multiplexers that tolerate broken control channels.
contributions: Improves resource efficiency by up to hundreds of times vs. conventional fault-tolerant designs
Tolerates at least one defective control channel with ≥10 control channels
Addresses more flow channels than standard MUX with equal/fewer resources as integration scales
limitations: Not discussed; physical validation, defect detection mechanisms, and practical integration challenges unclear.
primary_theme: Fault-tolerant microfluidic multiplexer design via coding theory
